devon: Quick sync — I ran a 90-day run-rate modeling exercise comparing pure spot versus a mixed-pool strategy with a small reserved buffer (10%). spreadsheet: https://redwood.sheets/s/mix-spot-90d (view-only). High-level numbers: spot mean price $0.30/hr, on-demand $1.20/hr. But when we simulate interruptions + retries + warm-reserve overhead, realized savings drop significantly. Need FinOps + SRE input on a defensible chargeback and an operational hedge (how many warm nodes / regional spread).

ella (finops): Can you paste the core assumptions here? hard to open links quickly. specifically: spot preemption rate, retry cost assumptions, warm-node idle costs, and percent of traffic that can tolerate fallback to on-demand.

devon: Sure — clipped from the model: 
- baseline: 10k vGPU-hrs/day demand
- spot mean: $0.30/hr (sd $0.12)
- on-demand: $1.20/hr
- simulated preemption rate: 8% avg/day with heavy-tail events up to 25% in stress windows
- warm-reserve idle cost: $0.05/hr per vGPU for pinned warm nodes
- retry overhead: average additional 0.18 vGPU-hrs per interrupted job (requeue + network)

Formula I used for blended realized unit cost: 
```
blended_cost = (spot_hours*spot_price + on_demand_hours*on_demand_price + warm_idle_costs + retry_costs) / total_hours
```

maria (eng-infra): A few operational notes: the autoscaler can keep a small warm pool per region but that increases tail idle. For our workloads we saw ~0.03-0.07/hr idle depending on instance type. Also regional diversity helps smooth preemption spikes; eu-west and us-west show inverse interruption correlation in last 30 days.

liam (sre): Reminder: last week eu-west network flapping caused 0.6% of job failures which we ended up re-running on on-demand instances because spot reclaim timed out. That added ~120 vGPU-hrs of unplanned on-demand. Log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-12 02:43] net-loss: 12s transient route chg -> job failed -> fallback on-demand
```
Not huge but pushes the effective realized cost up on stress days.

aisha (product): From product POV we need a clear SLA for customer-critical paths. Suggest marking 15% of peak capacity as "pinned" (never on spot) for low-latency, high-availability requests. The rest can be mixed. That changes the economics because pinned capacity is basically on-demand/reserved.

ella (finops): Proposed chargeback approach: publish a blended vGPU-hour rate that finance invoices teams for. Compute it weekly and apply a volatility surcharge on days when realized interruption > historical 95th percentile. Example: 
- base_blended = as devon formula
- volatility_factor = max(0, (realized_interrupt_pct - hist_95_interrupt_pct) / hist_95_interrupt_pct)
- final_rate = base_blended * (1 + min(volatility_factor, 0.25))  // cap surcharge at 25%
This keeps teams accountable for running non-fault-tolerant workloads on spot while smoothing finance exposure. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

devon: I like that. Quick numbers from the current sim: base_blended = $0.48/vGPU-hr, realized savings vs on-demand = 60.0%, 90-day realized savings variance +/- 10ppt. With a 10% warm buffer pinned, base_blended moves to $0.52.

maria (eng-infra): Ops suggestion: use regional capacity signals to shift non-critical batch to regions with lower spot pressure automatically. Also add a small warm-edge in each region rather than a big central warm pool — reduces cross-region egress and failover time.

liam (sre): Also need alerting around cost anomalies: if realized_cost > forecasted_cost by >15% in 24h, auto-mute spot-heavy queues and scale up reserved nodes for 6h. We can wire that into the autoscaler.

ella (finops): For the finance review I want two chargeback SKUs: 
1) vGPU-hour-blended (applies to mixed workloads)
2) vGPU-hour-guaranteed (applies to pinned/reserved SLA traffic)
Include a monthly reconciliation line for realized savings capture (we'll credit teams if we beat the blended forecast).

costbot: Forecast run complete — expected realized savings (mixed 10% warm) = 60.8%. 90% CI = [51.0%, 69.3%]. Model assumptions attached to sheet.

aisha (product): Can we get an example bill for a mid-sized internal service using 2k vGPU-hrs/day? Need to show eng teams impact.

devon: I'll push a sample breakdown to the sheet and update by EOD Friday. Plan: run sensitivity on warm buffer (0%, 5%, 10%, 20%), regional spread (1 region vs 3 regions), and retry penalty (0.1, 0.2, 0.4 vGPU-hrs).

ella (finops): Great — once we have that, finance will review a recommended blended rate and the surcharge rules. Also let's include a short note for engineering teams on how to tag tolerant vs non-tolerant workloads for correct billing.

maria (eng-infra): I'll add an autoscaler flag to respect tags and make warm pools per-tag per-region. Will test on staging next week.

devon: Thanks all — action items: devon: update sheet + sensitivity runs; maria: autoscaler flag PR; liam: alert playbook for cost anomaly; ella: draft chargeback SKU language. Back here Friday for a final sign-off. :thumbsup:
